standard_statement: A Tauberian theorem transfers analytic boundary information about a transform into asymptotic information about an underlying summatory function, under explicit side conditions.

warning: Pole data alone are insufficient without monotonicity/positivity and boundary hypotheses.

route: boundary nonvanishing of zeta on Re(s)=1

statement: For logarithmic derivatives, zeros on the boundary create singularities that obstruct direct boundary regularity.

valid_examples: certified Tauberian hypotheses => certified main-term transfer
theta(x)~x => pi(x)~x/log x via partial summation
invalid_reversals: observed main term on finite range => boundary nonvanishing
pi(x) approximately x/log x numerically => PNT proof
functional equation symmetry => Tauberian boundary regularity

forward: PVG-labelled prime-power points supply Lambda coefficients and cumulative observables such as psi.
analytic_layer: Tauberian transfer acts on a global transform and boundary behavior, not locally on valuation coordinates.
loss: Aggregated asymptotics do not recover individual valuation points or zero locations.
